questions.text: Choose the sentence with correct subject–verb agreement.
options: The list of laboratory tasks are on the desk.
The list of laboratory tasks is on the desk.
The list of laboratory tasks were on the desk.
The list of laboratory tasks have been on the desk.

questions.text: Which reading technique is best when you need to locate a specific date in a long report without reading every sentence?
options: Scanning
Skimming
Predicting the conclusion without reading
Paraphrasing the whole report

questions.text: Choose the correct completion: “If the team ___ the instructions carefully, it will avoid the error.”
options: read yesterday
had read
reads
was read

questions.text: A passage says the new lab reduced processing time, but it does not state whether costs also fell. Which conclusion is justified?
options: Costs definitely fell because time fell
Costs must have increased
The lab is more expensive than the old lab
Processing time fell; the passage gives insufficient evidence about cost

questions.text: You must email a faculty member to request clarification about one assignment requirement. Which subject line is clearest and most professional?
options: URGENT!!! PLEASE READ
Question
Clarification requested: Assignment 2, requirement 3
I don't understand anything

questions.text: A student summarizes a passage by copying three examples but omitting the author's main claim. Which reading skill should be improved first?
options: Identifying the central idea and distinguishing it from supporting details
Reading every word aloud
Memorizing the examples in order
Searching only for unfamiliar words

questions.text: A report states: “Although attendance increased, the survey response rate fell; therefore, satisfaction improved.” What is the main reasoning flaw?
options: It uses a contrast word incorrectly in every possible context
It assumes increased attendance proves satisfaction improved, despite the response-rate limitation and no direct satisfaction evidence
It contains no dependent clause
It uses the past tense

questions.text: Choose the revision that preserves the intended meaning and removes the ambiguous pronoun: “When Nisha spoke to Riya after she submitted the report, she was worried.”
options: After submitting the report, Nisha spoke to Riya, who was worried.
Nisha spoke to Riya after she submitted it, and she was worried.
After Nisha submitted the report, she spoke to Riya, who was worried.
Nisha and Riya submitted the report after she spoke to her.

questions.text: A comprehension passage says a pilot program improved results at two small campuses, while noting that larger campuses were not studied. Which inference is most defensible?
options: The program will improve results at every campus
The program has no value because the sample was small
The study proves campus size never affects results
The findings are promising for the studied campuses, but broader generalization needs further evidence

questions.text: An event report must be formal, evidence-based and concise. Which draft is strongest?
options: It records the purpose, date, participants, activities, observed outcomes and relevant limitations in neutral language
It focuses mainly on the writer's excitement and personal opinions
It lists every conversation verbatim but omits the event purpose
It states that the event was successful without observations or evidence
